## FILE: football-siam-weekly-content-masterplan__1_.md

# Football Siam — Weekly Content Master Plan (Thai League 1)

A working SOP for a full matchweek cycle: social templates + long-form. Built so most of it can run on autopilot once the Canva templates exist and the weekly data (fixtures, lineups, results, stats) is in front of me.

---

## 1. The weekly cadence at a glance

| Day | Output | Format |
|---|---|---|
| **Thursday** | Matchweek fixtures graphic | Social — Canva template, 1 post |
| **Friday AM** | "Eight Things to Look Out For" preview | Written + HTML (Divi block) |
| **Friday** | 30 mins pre-KO: Lineup graphic (per match) | Social — Canva template, ×N matches |
| **Friday** | Post-match: Result graphic + match report link | Social — Canva template, ×N matches |
| **Friday PM** | Matchweek results summary (running) | Social — Canva template, updated |
| **Saturday** | Same lineup → result → running summary cycle | Social, ×N matches |
| **Saturday/Sunday** | Player of the Day radar chart | Social — Canva template, 1 per day |
| **Sunday** | Same lineup → result → final summary cycle | Social, ×N matches |
| **Sunday PM** | Final matchweek results summary | Social — Canva template |
| **Monday** | Team of the Week | Social — Canva template |
| **Monday** | "Eight Talking Points" review | Written + HTML (Divi) + Substack cross-post |
| **Rolling** | Print interview (weekly) | Written + HTML |
| **Rolling** | Deep dive (weekly) | Written + HTML |

Everything social is built around **one Canva template family, reused and refilled** — same approach as the Chelsea graphics you sent (bold sans headline, brand-yellow-equivalent accent, club crests, dark stadium/crowd backdrop). For Football Siam I'd anchor the accent colour to the site's `#004d25` bottle green rather than yellow, crests in place of the Chelsea/Fulham badges.

---

## 2. Social templates — spec sheet

For each, I've listed what stays fixed in the Canva template vs. what I'd fill in weekly. Canva's connected to this account, so once templates exist as reusable Canva designs, I can autofill data fields into them directly and export — no manual re-typing of scorelines needed.

### 2.1 Matchweek Fixtures (Thursday)
- **Fixed:** "Fixtures" headline, matchweek badge, T1 league logo, layout grid for 8 fixtures (T1 has 16 clubs / 8 games a week).
- **Filled weekly:** matchweek number, each fixture's two crests, venue (H/A framed from a lead club or just neutral list), date, kickoff time (Thai local, ICT).
- **Source:** T1 official fixture list / club fixture pages.

### 2.2 Pre-match Lineup (30 mins before KO, per game)
- **Fixed:** "Starting XI" headline treatment, both crests top corners, numbered list layout, "Substitutes" footer band — mirrors the Chelsea graphic structure closely.
- **Filled per match:** confirmed XI with squad numbers, captain marker, subs bench.
- **Source:** FootyStats, per match. One caveat carried over from the T1 season preview project: FootyStats has previously returned inconsistent data (mixed sample sizes/seasons) for some clubs, so worth a quick sanity check on the page before pulling lineup data into a graphic, especially early in the window before its T1 coverage has settled for the season.

### 2.3 Post-match Result (per game)
- **Fixed:** "Full-time" banner treatment, big scoreline numerals either side, both crests, "+" divider ticks — again close to the Chelsea template.
- **Filled per match:** final score, scorers (optional strip), a call-to-action linking to the match report URL.
- **Source:** FootyStats once the final whistle goes; match report link once written/published.

### 2.4 Matchweek Results Summary (Fri/Sat/Sun evenings, rolling)
- Same base template as 2.1 (fixtures list), but each fixture slot updates from "kickoff time" to "final score" as results land through the weekend. Posted three times as the picture fills in — effectively the same graphic, incrementally completed.

### 2.5 Player of the Day radar chart (Saturday, Sunday)
- **Fixed:** radar/spider chart frame, 5–6 axes (e.g. goals/xG, key passes, dribbles, tackles won, duels won, pass accuracy), player photo/crest corner.
- **Filled daily:** one standout player's stats plotted, per your discussed format.
- **Source:** you'll send through player ratings for each game weekly — I'll use those to pick the standout and pull whatever underlying stats are needed for the radar axes. Worth settling exactly what data comes with the ratings (just a score, or a fuller stat line?) since the radar's only as detailed as what's in front of me.

### 2.6 Team of the Week (Monday)
- As discussed previously — pitch-graphic formation layout, 11 crests/names slotted into a formation shape, one graphic per week.
- **Source:** built from the same weekly player ratings — once I've got all games' ratings for the matchweek, I can shortlist the top performers by position and we settle the XI and formation together before it goes to the template.

---

## 3. Written content

### 3.1 Friday morning preview — "Eight Things to Look Out For"
Modelled on the Guardian's weekend preview format: one short, punchy section per fixture (not always the whole match — often a single sharpened storyline: a returning player, a tactical wrinkle, a managerial pressure point), numbered, wry and specific rather than generic preview-speak. With 16 clubs and 8 fixtures a week, this maps cleanly one point per game.

Delivered as: plain written copy + full HTML in your Divi/house-style template.

### 3.2 Monday review — "Eight Talking Points"
Modelled on the Guardian's Monday "talking points from the weekend" piece: retrospective, thematic — refereeing decisions, form swings, a manager under pressure, a breakout performance, table implications. With 8 games a week this also maps one point per game, though it's fine to occasionally group two matches under a shared theme (relegation six-pointer, title-race implications) if that serves the piece better than forcing 8 separate ones. Each point links out to the relevant match report and/or highlights video.

Delivered as: plain written copy + full HTML (Divi) + a version formatted for Substack cross-posting with a link back to the Football Siam page.

### 3.3 Weekly print interview
Standard long-form Q&A/profile format in house style — need a subject and access confirmed each week; I can draft questions, structure, and the write-up once you've got the conversation (or a pre-existing quote source) to work from.

### 3.4 Weekly deep dive
One subject per week — tactical trend, club history, a data story, a policy/governance issue in Thai football. Same house HTML treatment, longer-form, can use the `.dynamic-section` / tabbed / accordion components where the subject has natural sub-sections (e.g. a multi-club data comparison).

---

## 4. What I need from you to make this run smoothly

1. **Lineups and live results** — covered, via FootyStats. Worth noting I still can't monitor a feed in the background between messages, so the trigger to pull the lineup/result and build the graphic still needs a quick ping from you at the right moment (30 mins pre-KO, full-time) rather than this happening with zero prompting.
2. **Weekly player ratings** — you send these through each week (per game); I'll use them to work out player of the day and shortlist the Team of the Week XI with you. Useful to know upfront whether these will come as a simple score-per-player or something with more stat detail attached, since that shapes what the radar chart can actually show.
3. **Canva templates built from the specs in Section 2** — once you've made these in Canva, tell me and I can pull design IDs/fields directly via the Canva connection and autofill them each week rather than you rebuilding from scratch.

---

## 5. House style reminders (carried from existing brief)

- UK English throughout, Guardian/Athletic register — considered, wry where it earns it, never forced.
- Every written piece delivered in **both** plain copy and full HTML using the existing `#004d25` house template (byline bar, `.dynamic-section`, accordion/tab components as needed).
- Images: WordPress MCP image upload only works from public URLs — logos/photos still go through manual wp-admin upload, with `INSERT-URL/filename` placeholders substituted after.

## FILE: football-siam-team-of-the-week-automation-plan.md

# Football Siam — Team of the Week Automation & House Style Plan

A companion document to the existing weekly content master plan, capturing the Team of the Week (TOTW) workflow, the Canva asset library setup, and the full house style guide as agreed.

---

## 1. Article writing standard (all written pieces)

- **Language:** UK English throughout.
- **Register:** Guardian / The Athletic style — considered, wry editorial prose in the mould of Barney Ronay or Jonathan Wilson. Never forced, never generic preview-speak.
- **Delivery:** every article is supplied in **two formats**, every time:
  1. Plain written copy (readable prose, no markup).
  2. Full HTML, formatted as a Divi block using the house style guide below.

---

## 2. Team of the Week — automation plan

### 2.1 Fixed requirements
- **Formation:** always 4-3-3 (1 GK, 4 DEF, 3 MID, 3 FWD) — non-negotiable per Simon's total-football/Cruyff preference.
- **Cadence:** every Monday, following the completed T1 matchweek (16 clubs / 8 fixtures).
- **Visual output:** a pitch-graphic formation layout with player photos and club badges slotted into position.

### 2.2 Data source — match ratings
- Source of truth for player form is **FotMob match ratings**, gathered across the weekend's 8 fixtures.
- **Known constraint:** FotMob has no public API. Automated scraping of the site would sit against FotMob's terms of use, so this cannot run as an unattended background job. The practical workflow is Simon supplying the ratings each week (screenshot, copy-paste, or a non-paywalled/non-scrape-blocked link), after which Claude selects the XI and drafts the accompanying analysis.
- This mirrors the existing note in the master plan: Simon sends weekly player ratings per game; Claude uses them to determine Player of the Day and shortlist the Team of the Week.

### 2.3 Image sourcing — the "build as you go" headshot library
- Player headshots are the main missing ingredient each week. Rather than re-sourcing photos from scratch every Monday, the plan is a **growing database**:
  1. Once a player is selected for TOTW, Simon finds/sources the headshot.
  2. Image gets uploaded into the shared Canva folder (see 2.4) or sent as a URL.
  3. Claude records a simple name → image lookup in persistent storage.
  4. Next time that player appears in a TOTW, the existing image is reused automatically — only new/previously-unfeatured players need a fresh photo search.
- Club badges are a one-off job by comparison (18ish clubs, not hundreds of players) and are largely already sorted — see 2.5.

### 2.4 Canva folder (asset host)
- Folder created: **Football Siam – Team of the Week Assets**
- Link: https://www.canva.com/folder/FAHUO88HD-E
- Folder ID: `FAHUO88HD-E`
- Purpose: holds club badges, the Football Siam logo, and (going forward) player headshots as they're sourced. Canva-hosted assets also solve the "needs a public URL" problem that both the WordPress uploader and Canva's own `upload-asset-from-url` tool share.
- **Important limitation:** Claude can only pull an image *into* Canva automatically from an already-public URL. Locally-held or base64 images (see 2.5) cannot be pushed into Canva by Claude directly — Claude will not publish private assets to a public host just to create a URL. These need to go in via manual drag-and-drop by Simon (Claude can supply each crest as a downloadable file to make this easy).

### 2.5 Club badge library — current status
15 of 16 current (2026/27) Thai League 1 crests are already saved (as base64 text files, ready to convert to PNG/JPEG and drop into the Canva folder):

Rayong, Uthai Thani, Sukhothai, Sisaket United, Ratchaburi, Rasisalai United, Prachuap, Port FC, Pattani, Pathum United, Lamphun Warriors, Chiangrai United, Chonburi (badge shown is a stylised "Sharks" shield — worth double-checking against Football Siam's own image library before formal use), Buriram United, Bangkok United.

**Gaps still open:**
- Ayutthaya United — not yet supplied.
- Football Siam's own logo (the green three-headed-elephant mark) — not yet captured as a file; drop it into the new Canva folder to close this gap.

### 2.6 Canva template — in progress
- Simon is building a dedicated **4-3-3 pitch layout template** in Canva (11 photo placeholders + 11 badge placeholders positioned by role: GK / back four / midfield three / front three).
- Once built, Simon will share the template name/link. Claude will then look it up via the Canva connection and autofill it directly each week, rather than hand-building the pitch graphic from scratch.

### 2.7 Weekly TOTW flow (once fully set up)
1. Simon sends fixtures/results + FotMob ratings for the completed matchweek.
2. Claude selects the XI (4-3-3) and checks the headshot database for existing images — flags any gaps.
3. Simon sources only the missing headshots and drops them into the Canva folder.
4. Claude autofills the Canva template (badges, photos, names) and drafts the accompanying write-up in house style.

---

## 3. House HTML style guide (full reference)

### 3.1 Palette
| Element | Hex | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Accent / brand primary | `#004d25` | Borders, active tabs, byline accents, blockquotes |
| Primary text | `#333333` | Body copy |
| Headings (H1–H4) | `#121212` | Strong hierarchy |
| Page background | `#fdfdfd` | Warm off-white |
| Container background | `#ffffff` | Panels, tables, accordions |
| Secondary background | `#f4f4f4` / `#f9f9f9` | Callouts, tab buttons, hover states |
| Muted meta / subtext | `#767676` / `#555555` | Bylines, timestamps, captions |
| Subtle dividers | `#dfdfdf` / `#eeeeee` | Borders on images, rules, tables |

### 3.2 Typography
- **Body:** Georgia, "Times New Roman", Times, serif — 1.1rem, line-height 1.6, margin-bottom 20px.
- **Headings/interface:** "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif.
  - H1: 2.2rem, line-height 1.2, margin 20px 0 15px 0.
  - H2: 1.6rem, margin 40px 0 15px 0.
  - H3: 1.2rem, uppercase, bold, tracked (used in dynamic boxes).
- **Byline:** 0.9rem, uppercase/bold author name, date aligned right.

### 3.3 CSS stylesheet (paste into `<head>`)

```css
/* --- Base Layout & Typography --- */
body {
    font-family: Georgia, "Times New Roman", Times, serif;
    line-height: 1.6;
    color: #333333;
    padding: 20px;
    background-color: #fdfdfd;
}

h1, h2, h3, h4 {
    font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
    color: #121212;
}

h1 {
    font-size: 2.2rem;
    margin-top: 20px;
    margin-bottom: 15px;
    line-height: 1.2;
}

h2 {
    font-size: 1.6rem;
    margin-top: 40px;
    margin-bottom: 15px;
}

p {
    font-size: 1.1rem;
    margin-bottom: 20px;
}

/* --- Broadsheet Byline --- */
.byline {
    font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
    color: #767676;
    font-size: 0.9rem;
    border-top: 1px solid #004d25;
    border-bottom: 1px solid #004d25;
    padding: 10px 0;
    margin-bottom: 30px;
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
}

.byline-author {
    font-weight: bold;
    color: #004d25;
}

/* --- Editorial Quotes --- */
blockquote {
    border-left: 4px solid #004d25;
    margin: 30px 0;
    padding: 10px 20px;
    background-color: #f9f9f9;
    font-style: italic;
    color: #555555;
}

/* --- Imagery & Captions --- */
.article-image {
    width: 100%;
    height: auto;
    margin: 25px 0 5px 0;
    border: 1px solid #dfdfdf;
    display: block;
}

.article-image-center {
    max-width: 500px;
    height: auto;
    margin: 25px auto 5px auto;
    display: block;
}

.image-caption {
    font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
    font-size: 0.85rem;
    color: #555555;
    margin-bottom: 25px;
    border-bottom: 1px solid #eeeeee;
    padding-bottom: 10px;
}

.image-caption-center {
    text-align: center;
}

/* --- Interactive Panels / Dynamic Sections --- */
.dynamic-section {
    margin: 40px 0;
    border: 1px solid #004d25;
    border-top: 4px solid #004d25;
    background-color: #ffffff;
    padding: 20px;
    box-shadow: 0 2px 5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05);
}

.dynamic-section h3 {
    margin-top: 0;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    font-size: 1.2rem;
    color: #004d25;
}

/* --- Interactive Tabs --- */
.tabs {
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 10px;
    margin-bottom: 20px;
    border-bottom: 2px solid #004d25;
    padding-bottom: 10px;
}

.tab-btn {
    padding: 8px 16px;
    cursor: pointer;
    border: 1px solid #004d25;
    background: #f4f4f4;
    font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
    font-weight: bold;
    font-size: 0.9rem;
    transition: all 0.2s ease;
    border-radius: 3px;
}

.tab-btn:hover {
    background: #e9e9e9;
}

.tab-btn.active {
    background: #004d25;
    color: #ffffff;
    border-color: #004d25;
}

.tab-content {
    display: none;
    animation: fadeIn 0.3s ease;
}

.tab-content.active {
    display: block;
}

/* --- Tables --- */
table {
    width: 100%;
    border-collapse: collapse;
    font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
    font-size: 0.95rem;
}

th, td {
    padding: 12px 15px;
    border-bottom: 1px solid #004d25;
    text-align: left;
}

th {
    background-color: #f9f9f9;
    color: #333333;
    font-weight: bold;
}

/* --- Accordions --- */
.accordion {
    background-color: #f4f4f4;
    color: #333333;
    cursor: pointer;
    padding: 15px 20px;
    width: 100%;
    text-align: left;
    border: 1px solid #004d25;
    outline: none;
    transition: 0.3s;
    font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
    font-weight: bold;
    font-size: 1.1rem;
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    align-items: center;
}

.accordion:hover, .accordion.active {
    background-color: #e9e9e9;
    border-left: 4px solid #004d25;
}

.accordion:after {
    content: '\002B'; /* Plus symbol */
    font-size: 1.5rem;
    color: #777777;
}

.accordion.active:after {
    content: "\2212"; /* Minus symbol */
}

.panel {
    padding: 0 20px;
    background-color: #ffffff;
    max-height: 0;
    overflow: hidden;
    transition: max-height 0.3s ease-out;
    border: 1px solid #004d25;
    border-top: none;
}

.fixture-row {
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    padding: 15px 0;
    border-bottom: 1px solid #004d25;
    font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
}

.fixture-row:last-child {
    border-bottom: none;
}

.fixture-date {
    font-weight: bold;
    color: #004d25;
    width: 150px;
}

.fixture-match {
    flex-grow: 1;
}

@keyframes fadeIn {
    from { opacity: 0; }
    to { opacity: 1; }
}
```

### 3.4 Reusable HTML components

**Article header & byline**
```html
<h1>Main Article Headline Goes Here</h1>

<div class="byline">

</div>
```

```

<div class="image-caption image-caption-center">Centered caption text.</div>
```

**Editorial pull quote**
```html

    <strong>Source Name:</strong> "Insert the impactful or official quote text here."
</blockquote>
```

**Accordion widget** (rules, timelines, rosters)
```html
<div class="dynamic-section" style="margin-bottom: 40px;">
    <button class="accordion">Section Title (Click to Expand)</button>
    <div class="panel">
        <div class="fixture-row">
            <div class="fixture-date">Label / Date</div>
            <div class="fixture-match">
                <strong>Primary Title</strong><br>
                <span style="font-size: 0.9em; color: #555;">Detailed description, fine print, or analysis.</span>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
```

**Tabbed content box** (categories, stats)
```html
<div class="dynamic-section">
    <h3>Data Category Breakdown</h3>
    <div class="tabs">
        <button class="tab-btn active" onclick="openTab(event, 'tab1')">All Items</button>
        <button class="tab-btn" onclick="openTab(event, 'tab2')">Specific Group</button>
    </div>

    <div id="tab1" class="tab-content active">
        <table>
            <tr><th>Field Name</th><th>Details</th></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Item Title</strong></td><td>Item description or analytical note.</td></tr>
        </table>
    </div>

    <div id="tab2" class="tab-content">
        <p><strong>Specific Group:</strong> Detailed textual summary for the secondary tab.</p>
    </div>
</div>
```

### 3.5 JavaScript (place before closing `</body>` when accordions/tabs are used)
```javascript
<script>
    // Tab switching handler
    function openTab(evt, tabName) {
        var tabcontent = document.getElementsByClassName("tab-content");
        for (var i = 0; i < tabcontent.length; i++) {
            tabcontent[i].style.display = "none";
            tabcontent[i].classList.remove("active");
        }
        var tablinks = document.getElementsByClassName("tab-btn");
        for (var i = 0; i < tablinks.length; i++) {
            tablinks[i].className = tablinks[i].className.replace(" active", "");
        }
        document.getElementById(tabName).style.display = "block";
        document.getElementById(tabName).classList.add("active");
        evt.currentTarget.className += " active";
    }

    // Accordion expanding handler
    var acc = document.getElementsByClassName("accordion");
    for (var i = 0; i < acc.length; i++) {
        acc[i].addEventListener("click", function() {
            this.classList.toggle("active");
            var panel = this.nextElementSibling;
            if (panel.style.maxHeight) {
                panel.style.maxHeight = null;
            } else {
                panel.style.maxHeight = panel.scrollHeight + "px";
            }
        });
    }
</script>
```

# Sources — "Every Club, Every Angle" (Thai League 1 2026/27 Preview)

Reference list for the giant T1 2026/27 preview (WordPress draft, post ID 25740: https://footballsiam.com/?p=25740). Kept here so future Football Siam pieces — season updates, individual club profiles, the next transfer-window round-up — can reuse the same sources without re-hunting for them.

## FootyStats — xG/xGA and club stats

Used for the "Underlying Numbers: xG and xGA by Club" table. **Caveat carried into the article itself**: FootyStats returned inconsistent seasons/sample sizes per club when fetched (some froze on the completed 2024/25 campaign, others on a partial run of recent 2025/26 matches) — treat any number pulled from these pages as a snapshot, not a verified full-season dataset, and re-check the sample size shown on the page before reusing.

## League table, club histories, coaches

Mostly Wikipedia — used for final 2025/26 standings confirmation, club history/foundation details, capacity figures, and coach attribution. Specific pages fetched and confirmed in this project:

- [Buriram United F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buriram_United_F.C.)
- [Port F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_F.C.)
- [Muangthong United F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muangthong_United_F.C.)
- [Rasisalai United F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rasisalai_United_F.C.) — note: this club's own page had an erroneous/unconfirmed coach table entry (Sirisak Yodyardthai) that conflicted with Chiangrai United's page; resolved in favour of Chiangrai United, whose own infobox and the coach's personal bio page both corroborate him there. Treat single-sourced Wikipedia coaching-table entries with caution.
- [Sisaket F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisaket_F.C.) — this is the old, now-defunct club, **distinct** from the newly promoted Sisaket United. Don't conflate the two in future pieces.
- [Kanchanaburi City F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanchanaburi_City_F.C.)
- Thai League 1 season/table pages, general: [Thai League 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thai_League_1)

Also used, for the Muangthong United relegation framing specifically: VnExpress (Vietnamese outlet, "disastrous season" quote) — exact article URL not retained from the original research pass.

## Transfers

Transfermarkt was the primary lookup tool requested by Simon for transfer facts (fees, ins/outs), cross-checked against Thai-language sports news where possible.

**Buriram United's full, corrected Ins list** was rebuilt in a later editing pass using **besoccer.com/team/transfers/buriram-united** as the primary source — the original piece had significantly under-reported the club's window (missed 8 real signings: Darlan Mendes, Nathan, Caju, Marc Navarro, Sebas Moyano, Alexandru Tudorie, Uroš Radaković, Jakkapan Praisuwan). Individual nationality/positional confirmation for those came from:
- Wikipedia player pages: Nathan (footballer, born 1995), Caju (footballer, born 1995), Sebas Moyano, Uroš Radaković, Alexandru Tudorie, Marc Navarro
- ESPN and Soccerway/ogol player pages, used to confirm Brazilian nationality for Port's Carlos Jatoba and Marcel Scalese (also under-tagged in the original draft)

**Ifeanyi Eze correction**: an earlier draft had a Nigerian forward, Ifeanyi Eze, signing for Buriram as a free agent ex-Wellington Phoenix. Cross-checked via **africasoccer.com**, which reported the move as never confirmed beyond speculative "linked with" coverage (transfer probability listed as "?"). A separate search snippet (friendsoffootballnz.com, blocked by robots.txt, title only) suggested he signed for an Iraqi Stars League club instead. Eze was dropped from Buriram's Ins list on this basis — flag this if his transfer status becomes clearer later.

If updating this piece or building the next transfer-window article, start at each club's Transfermarkt or BeSoccer transfer page — BeSoccer in particular proved more complete than Transfermarkt for Buriram's window and is worth checking first for other clubs too.

## Thailand national team (Anthony Hudson) — 2026 ASEAN Hyundai Cup squad context

Used to add context on Prachuap's Jehhanafee Mamah and Oussama Thiangkham, both of whom featured heavily for a Thailand squad that was much-changed at the tournament because clubs were reluctant to release players outside a recognised FIFA window, mid pre-season.

- **aseanfootball.org** — "I am pleased with the squad I have – Hudson" — source for Hudson's quote thanking clubs for their cooperation "even though it's a difficult time for each club during their pre-season," and for the squad-disruption framing generally.
- Soccerway / ESPN player pages — used to confirm Mamah's (6 caps, 1 goal — penalty v Myanmar, player of the match) and Thiangkham's (7 caps, effectively an ever-present) appearance counts at the tournament.
- **Bangkok Post remains inaccessible via WebFetch** (451 errors, apparent region restriction) despite surfacing in search results as a likely primary source for several Thai football stories this project touched (e.g. "Champions Buriram add 6 new stars," "Port and Uthai strengthen squads"). Worth trying again in future via a different access route if the site becomes reachable, since it's clearly a strong primary source for this beat.

## Style reference

Simon's brief referenced a Guardian-style "things we learned from the data" transfer-window piece as the model for Section Three and, in a later revision, for a data/chart-driven "five to watch" treatment (theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/03/deadline-day-deals-premier-league-transfers). **Both Guardian URLs given were blocked to WebFetch** (403 PROXY_REJECTED) and WebSearch couldn't surface the article content either — the resulting sections were built from general knowledge of Guardian data-journalism conventions (CSS bar charts, stat-chip rows, honest caveating) rather than the specific source article. Worth trying a different access route if a similarly-structured piece is commissioned again.

## Notes for reuse

- FootyStats club URLs above are the fast way back into per-club stats for any follow-up piece (mid-season review, run-in preview, etc.) — the numeric ID in each URL is required, plain slugs 403.
- BeSoccer's transfers-by-club pages (e.g. besoccer.com/team/transfers/buriram-united) are a good secondary check against Transfermarkt — this project found them more complete for at least one club.
- Where research in this project found a fact single-sourced or unconfirmed, that was flagged explicitly in the article copy itself (the "messy data" caveat) rather than smoothed over — keep that practice for future pieces given how thin Thai football's public data trail still is. The Ifeanyi Eze correction is the clearest example: a plausible-looking transfer that turned out to be unconfirmed, caught only by going back through the data a second time.

## WordPress editing notes (mcp-adapter-execute-ability / ewpa abilities)

Operational gotchas discovered working on post 25740, worth remembering for any future edits to Football Siam WordPress posts via this tool:

- `ewpa/search-replace`'s `search` parameter must not contain embedded newlines — multi-line search strings silently return "no matches found" even when the exact substring is verified present. Use single-line anchors only; multi-line content is fine in the `replace` value.
- A bare `</style>` as a search string triggers a "search text cannot be empty" error — avoid targeting closing tags in isolation.
- **Serious bug**: for some longer/more specific search strings (particularly ones combining an HTML tag prefix with plain text, e.g. `<div class="chart-bar-row"><div class="chart-bar-label">Germany`), the tool appears to match on stripped/plain text anywhere in the whole post, not just where the full tag context appears — causing the replacement HTML to be spliced in at multiple unrelated locations (e.g. into running prose, into unrelated fixture-row text) and badly corrupting the document. This happened twice in this project. **Safest practice going forward: for anything beyond a short, unambiguous single-line search-and-replace, prefer `ewpa/update-post` with a full `content` replacement** (fetch the current post, build the corrected full HTML locally, validate tag-balance with a script, then push the whole thing) rather than chaining many search-replace calls — much lower risk of silent corruption, and easy to verify with a byte-for-byte diff afterwards.
- Always re-fetch and diff/validate after any WordPress content edit, especially after search-replace calls — corruption can be silent (the tool reports success even when it inserted content in the wrong place).

## FILE: claude_assets_logos-b64_README.md

# Thai League 1 club crest library

15 of the 16 current (2026/27) Thai League 1 club crests, saved here as reusable assets for future Football Siam pieces — charts, graphics, social cards, anything needing a badge.

## Why base64 text files, not image files

This project's document store only accepts text content — there's no supported way to upload a binary image file directly via this tool. So each crest is stored as a single-line `data:image/png;base64,...` (or `image/jpeg`) string in a `.txt` file. To use one:

1. Read the file — the whole content is the data URI.
2. Either paste it directly into an `<img src="...">` tag (works as-is, no decoding needed), or decode the base64 portion (everything after the comma) back to raw image bytes for use in Python/PIL, a design tool, etc. Example:

```python
import base64
raw = open("chonburi.txt").read()
header, b64data = raw.split(",", 1)
with open("chonburi.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(base64.b64decode(b64data))
```

## Crest index

| uthai-thani.txt | Uthai Thani FC | JPEG |

If future branded graphics need the literal raster mark, ask Simon to attach it directly; in the meantime, on-brand graphics use the site's documented style-guide values instead (bottle green #004d25, Helvetica Neue headings) rather than a placeholder logo.
